title: Delta expands SAF access through multi-airport collaboration with Shell Aviation
summary: Delta plans to scale its use of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) across multiple U.S. hubs and priority cities with a five-year agreement with Shell Aviation set through 2030. The collaboration goes beyond conventional jet fuel supply and helps build the infrastructure, delivery, blending and logistics needed to help make SAF part of everyday flying. |
body_text: Sustainability Delta expands SAF access through multi-airport collaboration with Shell Aviation Delta plans to scale its use of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) across multiple U.S. hubs and priority cities with a five-year agreement with Shell Aviation set through 2030. The collaboration goes beyond conventional jet fuel supply and helps build the infrastructure, delivery, blending and logistics needed to help make SAF part of everyday flying. Staff Writer Jul 15, 2026 11:00am Delta Air Lines is scaling SAF through a multi-airport collaboration supported by Shell Aviation that aims to expand SAF availability and adoption. Together, the two companies will expand SAF availability across key U.S. hubs and priority cities — including Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Portland International Airport (PDX), John. F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Logan International Airport (BOS) and Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport (MSP) — while building the infrastructure needed to support long term, reliable supply. The collaboration comes at a critical time for fuel diversification and supply resilience. Under the five-year agreement, Delta plans to expand the supply of SAF through 2030, building on decades of collaboration on conventional jet fuel with Shell. The agreement builds on existing SAF initiatives between the two companies and is designed to support consistent fuel delivery — an essential step toward integrating SAF into routine airline operations, not a one-off milestone. “Current instability and uncertainty have made one thing very clear to consumers and businesses alike — supply diversity matters. With Shell, we’re proving that scaling SAF isn’t theoretical, it’s achievable,” said Amelia DeLuca, Delta's Chief Sustainability Officer. “This is about activating real supply chains at scale and creating a model that others can build on as we work across the industry to expand lower impact travel.” Roots to runway SAF Remote video URL Beyond expanding access to SAF, the collaboration focuses on how fuel reaches aircraft. Shell will support both blended and neat SAF deliveries at select hubs and priority cities, helping establish the logistics, blending and distribution capabilities required for dependable supply across Delta’s network. That infrastructure-first approach helps ensure SAF can scale with demand while maintaining operational reliability. “This collaboration delivers on today’s fuel needs and tomorrow’s aviation solutions. By supplying conventional jet, SAF and longer-term innovation, the deal will help strengthen energy security and contribute to the transformation of aviation,” said Reema Bari, Head of Aviation Americas at Shell. Our multi-airport and innovative approach looks ahead to the future of sustainable aviation. Delta and Shell will work together to evaluate and advance next generation SAF technologies — including alcohol to jet and power to liquid pathways — aimed at unlocking additional supply and further reducing lifecycle emissions over time. About Delta’s SAF Journey This strategic offtake builds on Delta’s broader SAF momentum, including its role as an anchor partner of the first-of-its-kind coalition, the Minnesota SAF Hub , with a commitment to implement an ambitious shared strategy for aggressively decarbonizing the airline industry by scaling SAF production and replacing conventional jet fuel. In 2024, for the first time in Minneapolis and Michigan’s aviation history, two 7,000+-gallon shipments of SAF arrived at both MSP and Detroit Metropolitan Airport (DTW) . Delta’s work to reach net-zero emissions by 2050 while delivering a more sustainable future of travel focuses on what we fly, how we fly and the fuel we use. With around 90% of Delta’s carbon emissions coming from jet fuel, SAF is the best and fastest known way to reduce carbon emissions in the near term on our journey to net-zero emissions by 2050. These partnerships and commitments demonstrate what collaboration across the entire SAF value chain makes possible — meaningful progress toward a more sustainable future for not just Delta, but the entire aviation industry. Read more about Delta’s collaboration with Shell in the Financial Times. Related Topics: Sustainable Aviation Fuel © 2026 Delta Air Lines, Inc.

title: ADT joins Requity for Baltimore Day of Service to support neighborhood revitalization and community safety
summary: ADT recently made $40,000 in donations and employees participated in a day of service to support Baltimore community safety.
body_text: ADT gave a $30,000 grant to Requity at the nonprofit's annual Day of Service event. ADT recently participated in Requity 's annual Day of Service in Baltimore, Maryland, joining employees, community partners and residents in hands-on neighborhood improvement projects designed to support long-term homeowners and strengthen local communities. As a long-time ADT Safe Places partner, Requity works to address blight remediation, neighborhood engagement, and resident support across Baltimore. The Day of Service represents the continued commitment between both organizations to create a visible, lasting impact in communities where it matters most. “ADT Safe Places is about helping people feel more secure in the places they live, work and build their lives,” said Quiana Pinckney, ADT's Vice President, Corporate & Brand Communications. “That mission comes to life through partners like Requity, whose hands-on work is creating visible, meaningful change in Baltimore neighborhoods. We’re proud to support that impact through both funding and employee volunteering, working alongside residents and community partners to help build safer, stronger communities.” ADT's participation included a $30,000 Safe Places partner grant to Requity and a $10,000 contribution to Signal 13 , the Baltimore Police Department Foundation. The combined $40,000 investment reflects ADT's strategy of concentrating resources in communities where established partnerships enable measurable, long-term impact. In addition to the grant, ADT employees participated in a full day of service alongside Requity staff and community residents. “Investing in your community matters,” said Michael Rosenband, Requity's Founder and Executive Director. “ADT has been a longtime partner, and we're grateful for the time, resources and support they continue to provide. It's encouraging to see a company not just talk about community, but actively invest in it. That commitment makes a lasting difference.” About ADT ADT is a leading provider of security, interactive and smart home solutions serving residential and small business customers in the U.S. Through innovative offerings, unrivaled safety and a premium customer experience delivered by the largest network of smart home security professionals in the U.S., ADT empowers people to protect and connect to what matters most, every second, every day. For more information, visit ADT.com . About Requity Requity Foundation Inc is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt, nonprofit corporation established to break down barriers between vocational education and the marketplace. We are transforming vocational education through work-based learning projects designed to build community wealth while advancing sustainability and resilience. For more about Requity, please visit its website at requity.org . body_text: Stran & Company Advances to No. 21 on ASI Counselor® Top 40 Distributors List July 24, 2026 8:30am EDT Download as PDF Recognition Reflects Continued Growth, Enterprise Client Expansion, and Strengthening Market Leadership in the Promotional Products Industry Quincy, MA, July 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Stran & Company, Inc. The annual rankings, compiled by the Advertising Specialty Institute (ASI), recognize the largest promotional products distributors in North America based on verified annual revenue. The Counselor Top 40 rankings are widely regarded as one of the promotional products industry's premier benchmarks, evaluating distributors solely on verified North American promotional products revenue. The 2026 rankings recognize companies that successfully navigated a dynamic operating environment while continuing to drive meaningful growth and innovation across the industry. "Our continued advancement in the ASI Counselor Top 40 rankings reflects the dedication of our team and the trust our clients place in Stran as a strategic marketing partner," said Andy Shape, President and Chief Executive Officer of Stran. "Moving up two spots in one of the industry's most respected rankings demonstrates the momentum we've built through disciplined execution, investments in innovation, and our focus on delivering measurable value to some of the world's leading brands. As we continue to expand our enterprise relationships and enhance our technology-driven solutions, we believe Stran is well positioned to build on this success and create long-term value for both our clients and shareholders." About Stran For over 30 years, Stran has grown to become a leader in the promotional products industry, specializing in complex marketing programs to help recognize the value of promotional products, branded merchandise, and loyalty incentive programs as a tool to drive awareness, build brands and impact sales. Stran is the chosen promotional programs manager of many Fortune 500 companies, across a variety of industries, to execute their promotional marketing, loyalty and incentive, sponsorship activation, recruitment, retention, and wellness campaigns. Stran provides world-class customer service and utilizes cutting-edge technology, including efficient ordering and logistics technology to provide order processing, warehousing and fulfillment functions. The Company’s mission is to develop long-term relationships with its clients, enabling them to connect with both their customers and employees in order to build lasting brand loyalty. Additional information about the Company is available at: www.stran.com . About ASI The Advertising Specialty Institute (ASI®, asicentral.com ) is the premier technology, marketing and information provider in the $27.7 billion promotional products industry. ASI’s flagship platform ESP+ connects tens of thousands of distributors and suppliers through a powerful, all-in-one system for product discovery, sourcing, presentations and online stores. Family-owned since 1962, ASI also delivers trusted industry news, research, shows, events and education that help companies grow. title: Imprinting Quality - Vitalize
summary: Design is the voice of quality, and part of the Vitalize experience.
body_text: Let’s talk about quality. Quality is viscerally known through the emotions we feel, visually prescribed by the elements our eyes lay on, and through the delight that our environments, including our tools, give us. We instantly know what that feels like, and it starts with the first look. The first look Psychologically, the weight of a first impression is immeasurable. Konrad Lorenz's classic experiment illustrates this. Newly hatched ducklings, bind to the first moving thing. Usually, it’s the mother duck. But in this experiment, they followed Lorenz, and continued to follow him even though they eventually saw their mother. The same phenomenon is true in human experience: the initial navigation of a product, the first glance of a physical space, the opening notes of a voice. These moments carve a perception of quality immediately that is often hard to change. Design is at the root of these encounters, and has the potential to establish the bar of quality within milliseconds. And these implications have cascading effects. The quality void in healthcare Healthcare deserves nothing less than the highest quality. Yet when thinking of quality through the lens of design excellence, we think of companies like Linear, Ramp, Stripe. Enterprise healthcare, by contrast, remains largely absent from consideration. It is unfortunate how the tools that carry the weight of the human condition; tools used for split-second, often life-changing decisions; are too often designed as an afterthought rather than as experiences worthy of the stakes they carry. Clunky interfaces of medical records. Poorly designed systems for charting. Confusing health system workflows to coordinate care. Spend a few hours in any healthcare environment and you’ll be able to point this quality void out. Our founding team lived in Tennessee, two minutes across our first hospital, for eight months and saw all of this firsthand. And when we started building Vitalize, it started with design. Our first enterprise deal was made without a single line of code written. Just a visual prototype. Design as the voice of quality Since then, we’ve always led with design as an instrument of quality. This manifests in three ways: Every designer and engineer fly to customers at least once a month, and deeply embed themselves into our users’ workflows. They uniquely understand the challenges of our users and by extension, are thoughtful contributors to product vision given their perspective of user context. Our product function is not an afterthought. While most enterprise healthcare companies are heavily sales-led, we thoughtfully balance strategic needs for execs (the buyers) with the real day-to-day challenges that the end-users face. We experiment on a weekly basis. Feature-based experiments. Vendor and software experiments. Cultural and organizational practice experiments. We’re probably trying (and failing) exponentially faster than any other enterprise healthcare company, on this pursuit of quality. Design is the voice of quality, and ultimately becomes deeply embedded in the Vitalize experience. This means that design is at the start of every conversation, from how the product is shaped to how our new hires are being onboarded. There is a clear bar for quality that is created and set by every single member of our team. When we hire, we look to answer the question: “does this person raise the bar for the team?” We don’t micromanage quality. It’s a standard we exude on day 1 that is felt viscerally on the team, in how we treat each other and our mission. It trickles down to how we take care of our customers, how we lead product, and how we continually chase better. If you’re looking to raise the bar of quality in healthcare, consider joining our team .

body_text: Use a strengthening shampoo as the routine foundation when hair is regularly exposed to brushing, heat, color, UV, friction, or frequent washing; add a repair-focused step when damage is already showing as brittleness, roughness, dullness, tangles, snapping, or split ends [1]. Hair damage builds over time, so prevention and repair work best as different jobs in the same intelligent routine, not as a one-or-the-other bet [1]. Quick answer: choose by the state of your ha ir The OLAPLEX wash-care decision is simple: support hair before damage becomes obvious, then bring in a targeted repair step when the signs are already visible. Olaplex N°.3PLUS Complete Repair Treatment fits when hair needs more than shampoo, as a 3-minute pre-shampoo treatment step for all hair types and damage types. [2] Hair feels brittle, rough, dull, fragile, or tangles more than usual [1] A repair-focused step plus a strengthening wash routine Cosmetic repair care can improve how damaged hair looks and feels, but it should not be treated as permanent biological healing. [1] Add N°.3PLUS before shampoo when damage calls for targeted repair support. [4] Ends are visibly split or frayed Trim what is fully split, then support the routine [1] Split ends cannot be permanently fused back into healthy hair by shampoo alone. [1] Use repair and strengthening care to support the look, feel, and resilience of the lengths that remain. [1] Hair feels weighed down, coated, or sensitive to certain formulas [1] Recheck formula type and cadence [1] Conditioning and strengthening formulas vary; the right routine should lower friction and improve manageability without creating the wrong feel for your hair. [1] Keep the routine focused: cleanse with Nº.4, then add treatment steps only when the hair condition calls for them. [4] What damage prevention can do before breakage shows Hair does not wait for a dramatic snap to start changing. Older lengths and ends live through repeated styling, brushing, washing, environmental exposure, color services, and heat [1]. Over time, that weathering can make the fiber more vulnerable to roughness and breakage. A strengthening shampoo earns its place when the goal is routine damage defense: cleanse without unnecessary harshness, help maintain a conditioned feel, and support smoother handling so hair is not fighting friction every time you detangle or style [3] [1] [2]. Conditioning agents are commonly used to reduce friction, improve detangling, reduce flyaway, and support shine. Shampoo pH and friction can also matter because higher friction between fibers may contribute to cuticle wear. That is where Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo is most relevant [2]. It is a concentrated, sulfate-free shampoo for medium-to-coarse hair that gently cleanses while repairing everyday damage, strengthening and reinforcing bonds, replenishing hydration, boosting shine, and helping defend against future breakage [1]. For hair that is not severely compromised but lives a full life (color, heat, brushing, workouts, ponytails, friction), this is the foundational wash step [1]. Nº.4 at a glance Detail Reader-facing meaning Brand OLAPLEX Product Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo [2] Category Strengthening, bond-support wash care [2] Role in this decision Routine shampoo foundation for everyday damage repair and future-breakage defense. [2] Supported claims Scientifically proven to repair and strengthen hair; powered by patented OLAPLEX technology. Strongest fit Hair that needs a regular cleanse with strengthening, hydration, shine, and bond support. [1] What not to expect Shampoo alone should not be treated as a complete fix for severe chemical, heat, or mechanical damage. [1] When a repair-focused formula makes more sense Switch from “maintain and defend” to “target and support” when the signs are already there: brittle lengths, rough texture, dullness, tangles that feel new, extra breakage, or visibly frayed ends [1]. Those are cues that shampoo may still matter, but shampoo alone may not be the whole answer [1]. Damaged hair fibers do not biologically heal like living tissue [1]. Repair-focused cosmetic care can help hair feel softer and easier to manage and may help reduce the look and feel of breakage within the limits of the formula; it should not be framed as permanently reversing all forms of damage [1]. N°.3PLUS Complete Repair Treatment is the OLAPLEX step for that moment [1] [4]. It is a 3-minute, protein-free pre-shampoo treatment (not a shampoo) designed for all hair types and all damage types, using patented OLAPLEX Bond Building Technology™ as a targeted repair step before cleansing [4]. If your hair is already showing damage, the smarter move is not to abandon a strengthening shampoo. It is to give repair its own place in the routine [1]. The practical comparison checklist Think in roles, not labels. “Strengthening” and “repairing” can overlap in beauty language, but the decision becomes clearer when you ask what job the product needs to do. [5] Decision point Strengthening shampoo Pre-shampoo repair treatment Stronger fit when Hair is exposed to routine stress but still feels manageable. [1] Hair already feels brittle, rough, dull, fragile, or breakage-prone. [1] Main job Cleanse while supporting resilience, conditioning feel, and future damage defense. [1] Give damaged hair a more targeted repair step before or alongside the wash routine. [1] Cadence Can fit into regular wash days when the formula and hair feel are right; not every strengthening shampoo is automatically ideal for every wash [1]. Use when the routine needs more than cleansing, with timing guided by the product’s use context. [1] What not to expect Shampoos shouldn't be treated as a complete fix for severe chemical, heat, or mechanical damage. [1] Repair formulas can improve how damaged lengths look and feel but are not a permanent fix for split ends; trimming removes the split portion. [6] OLAPLEX path Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo is the wash-day foundation for everyday damage repair and bond support. [2] N°.3PLUS Complete Repair Treatment is the pre-shampoo repair step when damage is already visible. [4] A note on protein-heavy strengthening formulas: “strengthening” does not always mean the same thing. Some formulas lean protein-focused, some lean conditioning-focused, and some lean bond-focused [1]. If hair starts to feel stiff, coated, or less manageable, reassess the product mix and cadence rather than assuming more strengthening is automatically better [1]. Conditioning science points to the practical goal: reduce friction and improve handling without creating the wrong feel for the hair. [1] Build the routine around the damage you actually have Start with the job your hair needs done today, then keep the routine sharp. [1] Cleanse with a strengthening foundation when hair faces regular stress. Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo fits wash days when you want cleansing plus everyday damage repair, bond support, hydration, shine, and future-breakage defense. [2] Add targeted repair when damage is visible. If hair feels brittle, rough, fragile, or unusually tangle-prone, work N°.3PLUS Complete Repair Treatment into the pre-shampoo moment when your routine needs a dedicated repair step. [4] Condition after shampooing. Pair Nº.4 with Olaplex Nº.5 Bond Maintenance Conditioner as the wash-day conditioner step. Apply to mid-lengths and ends, leave on for 1–3 minutes, then rinse well. Conditioning helps reduce combing force, improve detangling, reduce flyaway, and support shine, which is especially useful for weathered lengths and ends. [1] Dial down repeat stress where you can. Heat, color services, brushing, environmental exposure, and washing-related friction can all contribute to cumulative weathering, so product choice works best alongside gentler handling. [1] Trim what is fully split. Cosmetic care can improve feel and manageability, but visibly split ends need a cut if the goal is to remove the split portion. [1] Bring in a professional when the concern looks beyond cosmetic damage. If you notice sudden shedding, scalp discomfort, persistent irritation, or breakage that does not match your styling history, pause the product pile-on and get qualified guidance. Product, service, and entity claims use official sources; broader category and mechanism background uses the source type shown below. Claim type Source used Product/service claims Official product, service, or entity source [2] Category or mechanism background Scientific source [3] [5] Expert or professional guidance Professional, institutional, or technical source [1] FAQ Can I use a strengthening shampoo every wash? A strengthening shampoo can fit regular wash days when the formula suits your hair and scalp feel [1]. The better question is whether it leaves your hair clean, conditioned, flexible, and manageable, not stiff, coated, or rough [1]. Formula type and hair condition matter [1]. Which conditioner should I pair with Nº.4? Pair Nº.4 Bond Maintenance Shampoo with Nº.5 Bond Maintenance Conditioner as the wash-day conditioner step. Apply Nº.5 to mid-lengths and ends after shampooing, leave on for 1–3 minutes, then rinse well. Together, they form the OLAPLEX wash-day duo for breakage-conscious routines. [7] Can a repairing formula fix split ends? Repair-focused care can improve the look and feel of damaged lengths, but it should not be treated as a permanent fix for split ends [1]. Once an end is fully split, trimming is the cleanest way to remove that split portion. Is bond-building the same as protein? Not necessarily. Protein-focused formulas and bond-focused formulas are different approaches within strengthening and repair care [1]. N°.3PLUS is positioned as a protein-free pre-shampoo treatment using patented OLAPLEX Bond Building Technology™ [4]. Should color-treated or heat-styled hair use prevention, repair, or both? Often, both roles make sense: a strengthening shampoo for the routine foundation, and a repair step when hair shows brittleness, roughness, dullness, tangles, or breakage [1]. Heat, color services, and repeated handling can contribute to cumulative weathering, so match the routine to the level of visible stress. [1] When should I see a professional stylist or dermatologist? See a professional stylist when breakage, split ends, or chemical-service damage needs hands-on assessment before the next color or heat service [1]. Consider a dermatologist when the issue involves sudden shedding, scalp discomfort, irritation, or a change that does not look like ordinary cosmetic damage. [1] Bottom line Prevention is the foundation; repair is the response when damage has already raised its hand.
